site.name: tessera
site.summary: Tessera Fictional embedded SQL database official docs and function reference (PostgreSQL / DuckDB official-docs style). Pages - `index.html` — Docs home. Hero (title + slogan + Get started button + real syntax-highlighted SELECT SQL example); version switcher (v2.4 / v2.3 / v2.2 / v2.1); ⌘K search; three quick-start cards (Install / Connect / Your first query); 6 docs-section cards (Architecture / SQL Syntax / Functions / Data Types / Storage / Extensions); dark / light theme toggle. - `reference.html` — Reference main entry. **Three-column layout**: left deep TOC tree (Schemas / Tables / Views / Indexes / Functions [Aggregate / String / Numeric / Date-Time / JSON / Window sub-groups] / Operators [category sub-groups], nodes expandable / collapsible); center reference overview + popular links + v2.4 new-features callout; right-side on-this-page outline. - `function-date-trunc.html` — DATE_TRUNC function detail page (**canonical example spec**). Three-column layout; signature code block; parameter table; return value; 3 SQL examples with result tables (basic usage / GROUP BY pairing / nested EXTRACT); error-case callouts; collapsible version-history panel (added v1.0, microsecond un

run_plan.goal: Explore and critique the UX of the Tessera docs system, covering the main docs flow, reference pages, and key interactions across desktop and mobile.
run_plan.summary: Start with the home page (index.html) to validate navigation, theme toggle, and quick-start flows. Then explore the reference page (reference.html) and function detail pages (e.g., function-regexp-match.html, function-row-number.html) to check three-column layout, TOC, and code examples. Finally, verify mobile responsiveness and error-handling for failing pages (e.g., function-date-trunc.html).
assumptions: The site is a static docs site with no dynamic backend (except maybe search), so page loads should be fast except for failing pages.
The three-column layout on reference/function pages is consistent across valid pages.
risk_hotspots: small tap targets (per layout warnings, especially on mobile)

phases.title: Home Page & Core Interactions
phases.objective: Validate home page navigation, theme toggle, version switcher, and quick-start flows.
key_checks: Click theme toggle (🌓) to switch dark/light.
Interact with version selector (v2.4 / v2.3) to check responsiveness.
Click 'Get started' and 'View reference' buttons to verify navigation.
Test search button (⌘K) for interaction (even if search is dummy).
exit_criteria: All home page interactables tested, theme toggle works, version selector responds, navigation links to reference/index work.

phases.title: Reference & Three-Column Layout
phases.objective: Explore reference.html, check TOC, popular links, and three-column layout consistency.
key_checks: Expand/collapse left TOC (e.g., Functions > String sub-group).
Click popular links (e.g., DATE_TRUNC, REGEXP_MATCH) to check navigation.
Verify right-side 'On this page' outline and center content layout.
exit_criteria: Left TOC interactable, popular links navigate, three-column layout verified on desktop.

phases.title: Function Detail Pages (Valid)
phases.objective: Validate function detail pages (e.g., function-regexp-match.html, function-row-number.html) for content, code blocks, and examples.
key_checks: Check three-column layout (left TOC, center content, right outline).
Verify code blocks (signature, examples) and parameter tables.
Test 'Edit this page on GitHub' button (if present) for interaction.
exit_criteria: Function pages load with valid content, code blocks/syntax highlighting (if present) are visible, examples are formatted.

phases.title: Other Reference Pages (Operators, Data Types, SQL Select)
phases.objective: Explore operators.html, data-types.html, sql-select.html to check content structure and navigation.
key_checks: Check left TOC structure (e.g., Operators > Arithmetic sub-group).
Verify content organization (e.g., SQL SELECT syntax on sql-select.html).
Check for consistent three-column layout (if applicable).
exit_criteria: All target reference pages loaded, content structure verified, TOC interactable.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Error Handling
phases.objective: Test mobile viewport for key pages, validate small tap targets, and check error pages (e.g., function-date-trunc.html).
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport, re-test theme toggle, version selector, and navigation.
Check small tap targets (e.g., search button, version selector) for usability on mobile.
Attempt to load function-date-trunc.html again to check error handling (e.g., 404 or fallback content).
exit_criteria: Mobile viewport shows responsive layout, critical interactables (theme, version, navigation) work, error page (if any) has meaningful fallback.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages (excluding failing ones initially, then re-validate failing pages if possible).
coverage_targets.features: Exercise all visible controls (theme, version, TOC, buttons, links) on key pages.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks (navigation, theme, version, TOC) on mobile viewport for index.html, reference.html, and one function page.

notes: Failing pages (function-date-trunc.html, function-json-extract.html) need re-validation to check if load error is persistent or temporary.

observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub REGEXP_MATCH Test whether a string matches a regular expression using the RE2 syntax. REGEXP_MATCH evaluates to TRUE when pattern matches anywhere in the input string. Anchor with ^ and $ for full-string matches. Signature REGEXP_MATCH(string TEXT, pattern TEXT [, flags TEXT]) → BOOLEAN Parameters Name Type Required Description string TEXT required The string to test. pattern TEXT required A RE2-compatible regular expression. flags TEXT optional Optional flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 's' dotall, 'm' multiline. Return value TRUE if the pattern matches anywhere in the string, FALSE otherwise. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL. Examples 1. Simple match Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('service-12', '^service-\d+$'); Result regexp_match true 2. Case insensitive match with flag Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('ABC123', '^abc', 'i'); Result regexp_match true 3. Filter rows matching pattern Copy SELECT email FROM customers WHERE REGEXP_MATCH(email, '^.+@example\.(com|org)$'); Result email ana@example.com julien@example.org nora@example.com Errors Common errors: invalid_regex: malformed pattern (unbalanced parens, invalid escape). regex_timeout: pattern took longer than 100ms to evaluate. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Pattern cache size raised from 256 to 1024 entries. v2.0Switched regex engine from PCRE to RE2 for predictable execution time. Some lookbehinds no longer supported. v1.5Added flags parameter. v1.0Added in initial release. observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub ROW_NUMBER Assign a unique sequential integer to each row within a window partition. ROW_NUMBER is the simplest of the ranking window functions. Unlike RANK, ties do not share a number. Signature ROW_NUMBER() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...) → BIGINT Parameters Name Type Required Description OVER clause WINDOW required Defines the window. PARTITION BY is optional; ORDER BY is required. Return value BIGINT starting at 1 for each new partition. Examples 1. Number all rows by created_at Copy SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY created_at) AS rn FROM orders; Result id rn ord_001 1 ord_002 2 ord_003 3 2. Top-N per partition A common pattern: find the latest event per user. Copy WITH ranked AS ( SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY created_at DESC) AS rn FROM events ) SELECT user_id, type, created_at FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1; Result user_id type created_at u_001 login 2026-05-11 14:22:08 u_002 purchase 2026-05-11 12:45:01 3. Distinguishes ties (vs RANK) Copy SELECT score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS rn, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS rk FROM leaderboard; Result score rn rk 95 1 1 95 2 1 90 3 3 Version history 2 entries ▼ v2.3Parallel evaluation of partitioned ROW_NUMBER across cores. v1.0Added in v1.0. dom_summary.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub ROW_NUMBER Assign a unique sequential integer to each row within a window partition. ROW_NUMBER is the simplest of the ranking window functions. Unlike RANK, ties do not share a number. Signature ROW_NUMBER() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...) → BIGINT Parameters Name Type Required Description OVER clause WINDOW required Defines the window. PARTITION BY is optional; ORDER BY is required. Return value BIGINT starting at 1 for each new partition. Examples 1. Number all rows by created_at Copy SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY created_at) AS rn FROM orders; Result id rn ord_001 1 ord_002 2 ord_003 3 2. Top-N per partition A common pattern: find the latest event per user. Copy WITH ranked AS ( SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY created_at DESC) AS rn FROM events ) SELECT user_id, type, created_at FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1; Result user_id type created_at u_001 login 2026-05-11 14:22:08 u_002 purchase 2026-05-11 12:45:01 3. Distinguishes ties (vs RANK) Copy SELECT score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS rn, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS rk FROM leaderboard; Result score rn rk 95 1 1 95 2 1 90 3 3 Version history 2 entries ▼ v2.3Parallel evaluation of partitioned ROW_NUMBER across cores. v1.0Added in v1.0. observation.title: SELECT statement — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array SELECT statement SELECT is the workhorse of Tessera. Its clauses are evaluated in a fixed order even though they may be written in any order in the source text. Syntax SELECT [DISTINCT] expression FROM source [WHERE] predicate [GROUP BY] expression [HAVING] predicate [ORDER BY] expression [LIMIT] n [OFFSET] n WITH Common table expressions for readability and recursion. Copy WITH recent AS ( SELECT id, amount_cents FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-01' ) SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM recent; FROM Sources can be tables, subqueries, table-valued functions, or external file readers. Copy SELECT * FROM read_parquet('s3://bucket/orders/*.parquet'); WHERE Row-level filter applied before grouping. Supports any expression returning BOOLEAN. GROUP BY Groups rows by the listed expressions. SELECT items must be aggregates or referenced in GROUP BY. HAVING Post-grouping filter, evaluated after aggregates compute. ORDER BY Sorts the final result. Supports ASC / DESC and NULLS FIRST / LAST. LIMIT and OFFSET Restricts the row count. OFFSET can be expensive on large result sets — prefer cursor pagination. Performance tip. Push column projection and filters into your storage layer when reading from Parquet — Tessera's read_parquet applies predicate pushdown automatically when supported. Examples Copy -- Top spenders this quarter SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount_cents) AS total FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-04-01' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount_cents) > 100000 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 20; ON THIS PAGE Syntax WITH FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER BY LIMIT Examples © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. observation.title: DATE_TRUNC — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. observation.title: JSON_EXTRACT — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub JSON_EXTRACT Extract a value from a JSON document using a JSONPath expression. JSON_EXTRACT navigates a JSON document with JSONPath. The result is a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null). Signature JSON_EXTRACT(document JSON, path TEXT) → JSON Parameters Name Type Required Description document JSON required A JSON document. Strings will be auto-parsed if they contain valid JSON. path TEXT required A JSONPath expression beginning with $. Return value A JSON scalar or composite value. Use ::TEXT or ::INTEGER to cast to a SQL type. Examples 1. Extract a string field Copy SELECT JSON_EXTRACT('{"user":{"name":"Ana","plan":"pro"}}'::JSON, '$.user.name'); Result json_extract "Ana" 2. Extract from JSON column in table Copy SELECT id, JSON_EXTRACT(payload, '$.event.type')::TEXT AS event_type, JSON_EXTRACT(payload, '$.event.amount')::INTEGER AS amount FROM events WHERE JSON_EXTRACT(payload, '$.event.type') = '"charge.succeeded"'; Result id event_type amount ev_8Hk2nF charge.succeeded 2500 ev_M5kQ2nF charge.succeeded 1899 3. Array indexing Copy SELECT JSON_EXTRACT('{"items":[10,20,30]}'::JSON, '$.items[1]'); Result json_extract 20 Errors Common errors: invalid_path: malformed JSONPath expression. type_mismatch: attempting to cast a non-scalar JSON value to a primitive SQL type. Version history 3 entries ▼ v2.4JSONPath now supports filter expressions like $.items[?(@.price > 100)]. v2.2Improved index access performance for large arrays by ~3×. v1.5Added in v1.5. Related functions JSON_VALID JSON_AGG JSON_OBJECT JSON_ARRAY JSON_TYPE CAST ON THIS PAGE Signature Parameters Return value Examples Errors Version history Related © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Data Types Native and extended types with storage details. Storage Page format, WAL, snapshots, and replication. observation.title: Data types — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array Data types Native types supported by the Tessera storage engine, with storage sizes and value ranges. Numeric types Type Aliases Storage Range Default Notes TINYINT INT8 1 byte −128 to 127 0 Signed 8-bit. SMALLINT INT16 2 bytes −32,768 to 32,767 0 Signed 16-bit. INTEGER INT, INT32 4 bytes −2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647 0 Default integer type. BIGINT INT64, LONG 8 bytes −9.22e18 to 9.22e18 0 Signed 64-bit. REAL FLOAT, FLOAT4 4 bytes IEEE 754 single 0.0 ~7 decimal digits. DOUBLE FLOAT8 8 bytes IEEE 754 double 0.0 ~15 decimal digits. DECIMAL(p,s) NUMERIC 16 bytes p up to 38 0 Fixed-point, no rounding. observation.title: DATE_TRUNC — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. Related functions EXTRACT DATE_ADD NOW CAST CURRENT_DATE AGE © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.
